meta.description: Market research: AI spend and LLM routing

user.t:
READ-ONLY market research for an HONEST investor pitch. Use WebSearch/WebFetch to gather REAL, SOURCED data (cite every figure with source + date). Your knowledge may be dated; prefer web sources and label anything you can't verify as "estimate/unverified". Write results to C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\results\market-research.md and return a concise summary. Do NOT install/download/clone anything.

The product being positioned (position it HONESTLY): a LEARNED LLM ROUTER + retrieval/memory layer that sends each request to the cost-optimal model (cheap model for easy tasks, premium for hard), routes around failing models, and shares a fast vector memory across agents — reducing LLM API spend and improving reliability. It is NOT "neuromorphic", NOT a new model, NOT proven on production traffic yet. Do not overstate.

Research and report, with sources:
1. Market size: total enterprise/developer spend on LLM/AI API tokens over the last ~3 years and credible projections for the next ~10 years (TAM/SAM). Give ranges and cite analysts; flag where figures are estimates.
2. Competitors / is anyone already doing this? Cover LLM routing & cost-optimization players (e.g. OpenRouter, Martian, NotDiamond, Unify, RouteLLM, LiteLLM, Portkey, Requesty, and any others you find) — what each does, open vs commercial, and how a learned-routing + shared-memory layer would differ or overlap. Be honest that this is an active, competitive space.
3. Typical realised savings from model routing (what published benchmarks/vendors claim, e.g. route-to-cheaper-model %), with sources and heavy caveats.
4. Target customers/segments (AI-heavy startups, enterprises with large token bills, agent-platform builders) and the buying pain (token cost, reliability, observability).
5. A sourced per-token price comparison across a few common models (to ground a savings calculator) — current list prices with dates.
Honesty rules: cite or label everything; no invented numbers; explicitly note competition is strong and that our edge is unproven until validated on real traffic. End with a sober SWOT.

handback.t:
Full report written to C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\results\market-research.md. Every figure is tagged PRIMARY (read on the source page), SECONDARY (third-party page or search summary), or ESTIMATE (my own arithmetic). I installed and cloned nothing.

**1. Market size**
- Menlo Ventures (2025-12-09) puts total enterprise gen-AI spend at $11.5B in 2024 and $37B in 2025, a 3.2x rise. Foundation-model API spend was $12.5B in 2025. These come from a survey of 495 US decision-makers, so they are estimates, not billing data.
- Menlo's earlier LLM-spend figure went from $3.5B in Nov 2024 to $8.4B in mid-2025.
- Gartner's AI spending is about $2.7T in 2026, but that is mostly hardware and infrastructure. Its "gen-AI models" line is $28.3B in 2026 and $51.6B in 2027 (SECONDARY; the Gartner page returned 403).
- Ten-year forecasts are for the broader gen-AI market, and they disagree widely: roughly $0.68T to $1.2T by 2035, at CAGRs of 31-41%. I would not cite any single one as the TAM.
- My own TAM/SAM framing (ESTIMATE): TAM is the API-token spend a router could touch, roughly $12.5B in 2025. SAM depends on an assumed 20-40% routable share, which is pure assumption and needs validation. I did not produce a SOM, because that needs pilot data.
- Sanity check: OpenRouter ARR is about $160M (Aug 2026, per Sacra) at a ~5% take. That implies roughly $3B of annualized spend flowing through it.

**2. Competition is strong and consolidating**
- OpenRouter raised $113M at about $1.3B in May 2026. Bloomberg reported on Aug 16 2026 that Stripe agreed to buy it for more than $7B.
- Portkey was acquired by Palo Alto Networks for about $140M (announced Apr 30 2026, closed May 29).
- Martian raised $9M in 2024. A blog says it is "nearing $1.3B" (unverified).
- Not Diamond has a thin raise (a blog reports about $2.3M pre-seed in late 2025). It already offers learned routing and prompt adaptation.
- RouteLLM is the open-source academic baseline. LiteLLM, Requesty, Cloudflare and Vercel gateways, and Bifrost/TrueFoundry cover gateway, fallback and caching. I did not verify Unify's current status.
- Memory specialists Mem0 (about $24M raised), Letta (about $10M) and Zep overlap the shared-memory half.
- Fallback and failover are table stakes, not a differentiator. Our only plausible edge is bundling learned routing with shared agent memory. That is an untested hypothesis, and the technique has public prior art.

**3. Savings**
- Vendor and authors' own claims: RouteLLM reports over 85% cost reduction on MT-Bench at 95% of GPT-4 quality. On MMLU and GSM8K it reports 45% and 35%. Martian claims 20-97% and Not Diamond claims 20-40%.
- The neutral evidence is much weaker. LLMRouterBench (arXiv 2601.07206, 33 models) found several routers, including OpenRouter, do not beat the best single model. The best routers reached up to about 31.7% cost reduction, or up to about 4% accuracy gain.
- RouterArena (Rice University) found no router optimal across metrics. A blog says a leading commercial router ranked 12th, but I could not read the leaderboard to confirm.
- Suggested pitch stance: "benchmark savings range from about 30% to 85% depending on who measured; neutral studies show the low end or no gain; ours is not yet validated on production traffic."
- A fair calculator must compare against batch (50% off) and prompt-caching (90% off cache reads) baselines, or it overstates router savings.

**4. Segments and pain**
- Target segments, in order of fit: AI-native startups, agent-platform builders, then large enterprises.
- Cost pain is supported by Menlo's 3.2x spend growth and by Gartner's forecast that over 40% of agentic projects will be cancelled by 2027, citing escalating costs (SECONDARY).
- Claims that 73% of enterprises overran AI cost projections, or that agents use 5-30x more tokens per task, come from blogs and are unverified.
- Counterpoint from Menlo: only 11% of teams switched provider in a year, which limits multi-vendor routing demand.

**5. Prices (USD per 1M tokens, input/output, read 2026-10-04)**
- Anthropic (PRIMARY, platform.claude.com):
  - Fable 5.1: $10/$50
  - Opus 5.5: $4/$20
  - Opus 5 and 4.x: $5/$25
  - Sonnet 5.5 and Sonnet 5: $2/$10 (the planned rise to $3/$15 was cancelled)
  - Haiku 4.5: $1/$5
- OpenAI (SECONDARY; the page was read through a summarizer and I could not read OpenAI's marketing pricing page, which returned 403):
  - gpt-6-astra: $10/$50
  - gpt-6.1-sol: $2/$10
  - gpt-6-luna: $0.10/$0.50
  - gpt-5.4-mini: $0.75/$4.50
  - gpt-5-nano: $0.05/$0.40
- Google (SECONDARY, summarizer):
  - Gemini 3.5 Flash: $1.50/$9
  - 3.7/3.8 Flash: $0.75/$3.75, rising to $1.50/$7.50 on 2027-01-01
  - 3.5 Flash-Lite: $0.30/$2.50
  - 2.5 Flash-Lite: $0.10/$0.40
- Aggregator pages conflicted with OpenAI's official names and prices, so verify OpenAI and Google manually before shipping the calculator.
- Anthropic's 4.7+ tokenizer produces about 30% more tokens for the same text, so per-token comparisons across vendors understate real cost differences.

The report ends with a SWOT, a say/don't-say list for the pitch, and a source list. The main weakness is that the edge is unproven. The best next step is to replay a design partner's real request log against a best-single-model baseline and a cache/batch baseline.
